examples.ko: 부품의 소형화 덕분에 휴대폰이 훨씬 가벼워졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the miniaturization of parts, phones have become much lighter.
These days the competition to make home appliances smaller is fierce.
As miniaturization progressed, laptops got thinner too.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 카메라 소형화 기술로 유명해요.
examples.en: This company is famous for its camera miniaturization technology.

examples.ko: 1인 가구가 늘어서 아파트 평수의 소형화가 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: With more single-person households, the shrinking size of apartments is noticeable.
They say there is a limit to shrinking semiconductors.

explain: 반대말은 '대형화'예요. 기계, 부품, 기술, 집 크기 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 그냥 작아졌다고 말할 때는 '작아지다'를 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '대형화' (enlargement). It often appears when talking about machines, parts, technology and the size of homes; for something simply getting small, people say '작아지다'.

examples.en: The company miniaturized the device and lowered the price too.
The research team shrank the sensor to the size of a fingernail.
To make the parts smaller, you need new materials.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 내년까지 장비를 소형화할 계획이에요.
examples.en: Our team plans to downsize the equipment by next year.

examples.ko: 어떻게 하면 배터리를 소형화할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: How can we make the battery smaller?

examples.ko: 자동차를 소형화하는 추세라서 작은 모델이 인기예요.
examples.en: There is a trend of downsizing cars, so small models are popular.

explain: '~을 소형화하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요. 저절로 작아질 때는 '작아지다'를 쓰고, 반대말은 '대형화하다'예요.
explain_en: Use it with an object, as in '~을 소형화하다'. When something just becomes small on its own, say '작아지다'. Its opposite is '대형화하다'.

examples.en: When you eat, digestive fluid comes out inside your body.
Thanks to digestive fluid, food is broken down into small pieces.
Saliva is also one of the digestive fluids.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 소화액이 나오는 곳을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class, we learned where digestive fluids come from.

examples.ko: 소화액이 부족하면 속이 더부룩할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you lack digestive fluid, your stomach can feel heavy and bloated.

examples.ko: 위에서 나오는 소화액은 아주 강한 산성이에요.
examples.en: The digestive fluid from the stomach is strongly acidic.

explain: 구체적으로 말할 때는 '위액', '침', '쓸개즙'처럼 이름을 직접 써요. '소화액'은 과학 수업이나 건강 설명에서 이것저것을 묶어 말할 때 많이 나와요.
explain_en: When being specific, people name the fluid directly, such as '위액' (gastric juice), '침' (saliva) or '쓸개즙' (bile). '소화액' appears mostly in science classes and health explanations when grouping them together.

examples.en: A summons arrived from the court yesterday.

examples.ko: 소환장을 받으면 정해진 날짜에 출석해야 해요.
examples.en: If you receive a summons, you must appear on the set date.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 소환장을 무시하고 나타나지 않았어요.
examples.en: He ignored the summons and did not show up.
They say the police sent a summons to the witness.

examples.ko: 우편함에 소환장 같은 서류가 들어 있어서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised to find a document like a summons in the mailbox.

examples.ko: 소환장에 적힌 시간에 맞춰 법원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the court at the time written on the summons.

explain: '소환장을 받다/보내다/발부하다'처럼 써요. 법원이나 검찰에서 오는 공식 서류라서 일상 대화보다 뉴스에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '소환장을 받다/보내다/발부하다'. Because it is an official document from a court or prosecutors' office, you meet it more in the news than in daily talk.

examples.en: The CEO shared his thoughts ahead of his retirement.
The winning player briefly shared how he felt.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 고향에 와서 느낀 소회가 남달라요.
examples.en: What I feel after coming back to my hometown after so long is special.

examples.ko: 작가는 책을 마치며 소회를 글로 남겼어요.
examples.en: The author left his thoughts in writing at the end of the book.

examples.ko: 소회를 묻는 질문에 그는 잠시 말이 없었어요.
examples.en: At the question asking for his thoughts, he was silent for a moment.
Looking back on this year, how do you feel?

explain: '소회를 밝히다/전하다/말하다'처럼 거의 굳어서 써요. '소감'과 비슷하지만 더 격식 있는 말이라 기사나 공식 자리에서 많이 나오고, 친구와는 '느낌', '생각'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is used almost as a fixed set, like '소회를 밝히다/전하다/말하다'. It is similar to '소감' but more formal, so it appears in news and official settings; with friends people say '느낌' or '생각'.

examples.ko: 잠시 쉬었다가 속개한 회의에서는 예산안부터 다루었어요.
examples.en: At the meeting resumed after a short break, they dealt with the budget first.
We resume the meeting after lunch.

examples.ko: 비가 그치면 경기를 속개할 거라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the game will resume once the rain stops.

examples.ko: 정전 때문에 멈췄던 수업을 한 시간 뒤에 속개했어요.
examples.en: The class stopped by the power outage resumed an hour later.

examples.ko: 재판장은 내일 오전 열 시에 재판을 속개한다고 했어요.
examples.en: The presiding judge said the trial will resume at ten tomorrow morning.

examples.ko: 협상을 속개하기로 해서 양측이 다시 만났어요.
examples.en: They decided to resume the negotiations, so both sides met again.

explain: 회의, 재판, 경기처럼 중간에 멈춘 공식적인 일을 다시 이어 갈 때 써요. 일상에서는 '다시 시작하다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is used when an official event that stopped partway, such as a meeting, trial or match, picks up again. In everyday talk people often say '다시 시작하다' instead.

examples.en: Our team's strength is the fast break.
They scored in an instant with a fast break.
The defense collapsed against the opponent's fast attack.

examples.ko: 감독은 선수들에게 속공을 더 연습하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The coach told the players to practice the fast break more.

examples.ko: 이 농구팀은 속공 한 번에 역전했어요.
examples.en: This basketball team turned the game around with one fast break.

examples.ko: 빠른 선수가 있어서 속공이 잘 돼요.
examples.en: We have a fast player, so our fast breaks work well.

explain: 농구, 축구 같은 구기 종목에서 수비가 자리 잡기 전에 빠르게 공격하는 것을 말해요. '속공을 펼치다', '속공으로 점수를 내다'처럼 스포츠 중계에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: In ball sports like basketball and soccer, it means attacking fast before the defense is set. You often hear it in sports broadcasts, as in '속공을 펼치다' or '속공으로 점수를 내다'.

examples.ko: 회의 속기록은 누구나 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can read the transcript of the meeting.
I found that remark in the National Assembly transcript.
After reading the transcript, I found the mood was different.
The trial transcript was released and became a hot topic.

examples.ko: 사고 경위를 속기록으로 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check how the accident happened in the transcript.
I confirmed the exact remarks based on the transcript.

explain: '회의록'은 회의 내용을 정리한 기록이고, '속기록'은 말한 것을 빠짐없이 그대로 받아 적은 기록이라는 점이 달라요. 국회, 법원 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '회의록' is a summarized record of a meeting, while '속기록' is a transcript written down just as it was spoken. It often appears in news about the National Assembly and courts.

examples.en: A stenographer is seated in the courtroom.

examples.ko: 속기사는 말이 끝나는 대로 빠르게 받아 적어요.
examples.en: A stenographer writes down speech quickly as soon as it is spoken.

examples.ko: 제 꿈은 국회 속기사가 되는 거예요.
examples.en: My dream is to become a stenographer at the National Assembly.
I attend a training school to get a stenographer's license.

examples.ko: 속기사가 있어서 회의 내용이 정확하게 남아요.
examples.en: Because there is a stenographer, the meeting is recorded accurately.

examples.ko: 속기사에게 발언을 천천히 해 달라고 부탁받았어요.
examples.en: I was asked by the stenographer to speak more slowly.

explain: '속기사 자격증', '법원 속기사'처럼 써요. '속기'는 말을 빠르게 받아 적는 일을 가리켜서, 법정이나 국회처럼 기록이 중요한 곳에서 일하는 사람을 말할 때 많이 들어요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '속기사 자격증' and '법원 속기사'. '속기' refers to taking down speech quickly, so you hear this word about people working where records matter, such as courts and the National Assembly.

examples.en: My friends are whispering at the back of the classroom.
The kids are whispering behind the teacher's back.
What are you two whispering about?
The sound of whispering in the theater bothered me a little.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 구석에서 속닥거리다가 웃음을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: The two were whispering in the corner and then burst out laughing.

examples.ko: 동생들이 밤새 속닥거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My younger siblings whispered all night, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: 작은 목소리로 은밀하게 계속 이야기하는 모습에 써요. 비슷한 말로 '소곤거리다'가 있고, 활용은 '속닥거려요', '속닥거리는'이에요.
explain_en: It describes talking on and on in a small, secretive voice. '소곤거리다' is a similar word, and it conjugates as '속닥거려요' and '속닥거리는'.

examples.en: The kids are whispering secrets to each other.
I can hear whispering from the back seats.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 귀를 맞대고 속닥속닥 이야기해요.
examples.en: The two put their heads together and talk in whispers.
I got scolded for whispering during class.

examples.ko: 방 안에서 속닥속닥 말하는 소리가 나요.
examples.en: I can hear the sound of whispering in the room.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 귀에 대고 속닥속닥 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend whispered into my ear.

explain: '속닥속닥 이야기하다/말하다'처럼 뒤에 말하는 동사와 함께 써요. 비슷한 말로 '소곤소곤'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used with verbs of speaking, as in '속닥속닥 이야기하다/말하다'. '소곤소곤' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 의사는 증상만 듣고 속단하지 말고 검사부터 해 보자고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said not to jump to conclusions from symptoms alone and to start with a test.
I jumped to a conclusion based only on rumors and made the misunderstanding worse.

examples.ko: 아직 결과도 안 나왔는데 속단하기는 일러요.
examples.en: The results aren't even out yet, so it's too early to jump to conclusions.

examples.ko: 사람을 겉모습만 보고 속단하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't judge people hastily by their looks alone.

examples.ko: 한 번 실패했다고 자신을 속단하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't write yourself off just because you failed once.
I concluded too quickly and regretted it later.

explain: '속단하지 마세요', '속단하기는 일러요'처럼 부정이나 조심하라는 말과 자주 써요. '단정하다'와 비슷하지만 '속단하다'는 충분히 보지 않고 서둘러 판단한다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is often used with negatives or warnings, as in '속단하지 마세요' and '속단하기는 일러요'. It is close to '단정하다', but '속단하다' carries the feeling of judging in a hurry without looking closely enough.

examples.ko: 저는 속독을 배워서 책을 빨리 읽어요.
examples.en: I learned speed reading, so I read books quickly.
Many students attend speed reading academies.

examples.ko: 속독으로 읽으면 내용이 잘 기억나지 않아요.
examples.en: If I read by speed reading, I don't remember the content well.
Speed reading skill helps in exams.

examples.ko: 속독은 연습하면 누구나 늘 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can improve at speed reading with practice.

examples.ko: 천천히 음미할 책이라서 속독은 맞지 않아요.
examples.en: It's a book to savor slowly, so speed reading doesn't suit it.

explain: 반대말은 '정독'이에요. 빨리 읽는 방법이나 학원 이야기에서 나오고, '속독법'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '정독' (careful reading). It comes up when talking about methods of reading fast or reading academies, and people also say '속독법'.

examples.en: I skim the newspaper by looking only at the headlines.

examples.ko: 시험 시간이 짧아서 지문을 속독해야 해요.
examples.en: The exam time is short, so I have to speed read the passage.
If you speed read a book, you only get the plot.

examples.ko: 그는 하루에 소설 한 권을 속독해요.
examples.en: He speed reads one novel a day.
I speed read only the important parts and skipped the rest.
I'm training so that I still understand even when I speed read.

explain: '책을 속독하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요. 반대말은 '정독하다'이고, 일상에서는 '훑어보다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It takes an object, as in '책을 속독하다'. Its opposite is '정독하다', and in daily talk people also often say '훑어보다'.

examples.en: He is a materialistic person who only cares about money.

examples.ko: 속물적인 생각이라고 비난받을까 봐 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't say it for fear of being criticized for a snobbish thought.
The movie satirizes the snobbish side of rich people.

examples.ko: 속물적으로 들릴지 모르지만 월급이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: It may sound materialistic, but salary matters most to me.
My friend's snobbish way of talking made me uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 겉으로는 속물적인 척해도 속은 따뜻한 사람이에요.
examples.en: He acts snobbish on the surface, but he is warm inside.

explain: '속물적인 사람', '속물적으로 들리다'처럼 써요. 돈이나 지위만 따지는 태도를 비판하는 말이라서 상대에게 직접 말하면 기분 나빠할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '속물적인 사람' and '속물적으로 들리다'. It criticizes an attitude of caring only about money or status, so saying it directly to someone can offend them.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 속사포처럼 말해서 알아듣기 힘들어요.
examples.en: He talks like a machine gun, so he is hard to understand.
The rapper rattled off a rapid-fire rap.
My younger sibling fired off questions one after another.
I was overwhelmed by the rapid-fire nagging.
When I'm nervous in an interview, I end up talking really fast.

examples.ko: 속사포로 설명하지 말고 천천히 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't explain at breakneck speed; speak slowly.

explain: 원래는 빠르게 연속으로 쏘는 대포를 말하지만, 지금은 말이 아주 빠르거나 질문, 잔소리가 쏟아지는 모습에 '속사포처럼'으로 많이 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 총을 연속으로 쏘듯 말이 쉴 새 없이 빠르게 나오는 모습이에요. 듣는 사람이 따라가기 힘들다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Words come out nonstop like rapid gunfire, with the feeling that the listener can hardly keep up.

explain_en: It originally refers to a quick-firing gun, but now it is mostly used as '속사포처럼' for very fast speech or a flood of questions and nagging.

examples.en: The kids whisper into each other's ears.

examples.ko: 바람이 나뭇잎 사이에서 속삭거리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems like the wind is whispering among the leaves.
The students who were whispering in the library went quiet.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 누가 속삭거리는지 자꾸 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: I keep wondering who is whispering behind me.
I whispered with my friend all night and went to bed late.
What are you two whispering about?

explain: 기본형은 '속삭이다'이고 더 많이 써요. '-거리다'가 붙으면 속삭이는 일이 계속되는 느낌이 나고, 비슷한 말로 '소곤거리다'가 있어요.
explain_en: The basic form is '속삭이다', which people use more. Adding '-거리다' gives the feeling that the whispering keeps going, and '소곤거리다' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 그는 속세를 떠나 산속 절에서 살아요.
examples.en: He left the secular world and lives in a mountain temple.
It isn't easy to give up worldly desires.
They say the monk cut his ties with the secular world.

examples.ko: 가끔은 속세를 벗어나 조용히 쉬고 싶어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I want to escape the busy world and rest quietly.

examples.ko: 속세에서 사는 사람들은 늘 바쁘게 지내요.
examples.en: People living in the everyday world are always busy.

examples.ko: 속세에 지친 주인공이 산으로 떠나는 이야기예요.
examples.en: It's a story about a protagonist tired of the world who goes off to the mountains.

explain: 절이나 산속 같은 조용한 곳, 종교 생활과 대비해서 '속세를 떠나다/벗어나다'처럼 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '세상'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used in contrast to quiet places like temples and mountains or to religious life, often as '속세를 떠나다/벗어나다'. In everyday talk people simply say '세상'.

en: swift and decisive action; quick finish

examples.en: We have to finish this job quickly and decisively.
The meeting was run in a quick, decisive way.

examples.ko: 팀장님은 속전속결을 좋아해서 일을 미루지 않아요.
examples.en: Our team leader likes swift action and never puts things off.
Quick and decisive is not always good.
I was surprised the negotiation wrapped up so swiftly.
The opponent was weak, so the blitz strategy worked.

explain: '속전속결로 끝내다/처리하다/진행되다'처럼 써요. 일이나 싸움을 한 번에 빨리 끝낸다는 말이라, 문맥에 따라 칭찬일 수도 있고 서두른다는 비판일 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used as in '속전속결로 끝내다/처리하다/진행되다', meaning finishing a task or fight quickly in one go. Depending on context it can be praise or a criticism of rushing.

examples.en: The passing of time is helpless and hard to stop.
There are things that are hopeless no matter how hard you try.
Time is merciless, and before I knew it my hair had turned white.
After a hopeless wait, he gave up.
Regretting it now is futile.

examples.ko: 속절없는 마음은 말로 다 표현이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The helpless feeling can't be fully put into words.

explain: 어떻게 해 볼 방법이 없어서 허무하고 안타까운 느낌이에요. 일상 대화보다 글이나 노래 가사에서 많이 보고, 활용은 '속절없어요', '속절없는'이에요.
explain_en: It carries a feeling of emptiness and regret at having no way to do anything about something. You see it more in writing and song lyrics than in daily talk, and it conjugates as '속절없어요' and '속절없는'.

examples.en: Time passed by helplessly.
The flowers withered away, and nothing could be done.
The team collapsed helplessly in the second half.
I waited in vain, and the whole day was gone.
Children grow up before you can do anything about it.

examples.ko: 한 번 놓친 기회는 속절없이 사라져요.
examples.en: An opportunity once missed vanishes beyond recall.

explain: 시간, 세월, 꽃이 지는 것처럼 막을 수 없는 일과 자주 써요. 일상 대화보다 글이나 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It goes often with things you cannot stop, like time, years or flowers falling. It appears more in writing and stories than in daily conversation.

examples.en: The employee who became the scapegoat for the accident felt wronged.
He was the scapegoat who took the blame for the team's failure.

examples.ko: 누군가를 속죄양으로 삼는다고 문제가 해결되지는 않아요.
examples.en: Making someone a scapegoat doesn't solve the problem.
An atmosphere of looking for a scapegoat spread through the company.
Why do I have to be the scapegoat?

examples.ko: 어린 동생이 형의 잘못 때문에 속죄양이 됐어요.
examples.en: The little sibling became the scapegoat for the older brother's mistake.

explain: 잘못이 없거나 작은데 남의 잘못까지 대신 책임지는 사람을 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '희생양'이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who takes the blame for others' faults though they did little or nothing wrong. '희생양' is a similar word.

examples.en: My mother thins out the lettuce in the garden.

examples.ko: 싹이 너무 빽빽해서 솎아 줘야 해요.
examples.en: The sprouts are too dense, so we have to thin them out.

examples.ko: 당근을 솎아 내면 남은 것이 더 크게 자라요.
examples.en: If you thin out the carrots, the remaining ones grow bigger.
My father is thinning the fruit on the apple tree.
I made kimchi with the thinned young radish.
When the seedlings grow, thin out the weak ones first.

explain: 그냥 '뽑다'와 달리 남은 것이 잘 자라도록 빽빽한 것 중 일부만 뽑을 때 써요. 상추, 열무, 과일 열매 이야기에 많이 나오고 '솎아 내다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '뽑다', it is for pulling out only some of a crowded batch so the remaining ones grow well. It is common with lettuce, young radish and fruit on trees, and you can also say '솎아 내다'.
